items.title: Ask HN: What will AI coding look like when today's CS freshmen graduate? (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: ChatGPT 3.5 only came out about three and a half years ago. Claude Code was released in February 2025. In one academic year, LLMs went from barely handling high school math to disproving unit-distance conjecture. Every two months we seems to have a new SOTA now. What do you expect AI coding to look like four years from now? Will it be like Go after AlphaGo, where even Ke Jie could only say "they no longer knew what they were fighting against"? Or will it just be like today, just stronger, with humans still driving the work and AI as a powerful assistant? Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48624855 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

items.content_text: In this tutorial, we build a complete Crawlee for Python workflow from setup to AI-ready output. We generate a local demo website, then crawl it with BeautifulSoupCrawler, ParselCrawler, and PlaywrightCrawler. We extract titles, metadata, product fields, and JavaScript-rendered cards, and capture full-page screenshots. We then normalize the data, build a link graph, and export JSON, CSV, and RAG-ready JSONL chunks. items.title: Cisco AI Introduces FAPO: Pipeline-Aware Prompt Optimization With Step-Level Failure Attribution and Claude Code Orchestration (Source: www.marktechpost.com | Category: Extras)
items.content_text: Cisco Foundation AI has open-sourced FAPO (Fully Automated Prompt Optimization), a Claude Code-driven system that autonomously optimizes multi-step LLM pipelines from baseline prompts to target accuracy. FAPO evaluates a chain, attributes failures at the step level, proposes variants across prompt, parameter, and chain-structure levels, and validates each through an independent reviewer. In Cisco's evaluation, it beat GEPA on 15 of 18 model-benchmark comparisons. Here's how the optimization loop works and how to run it. The post Cisco AI Introduces FAPO: Pipeline-Aware Prompt Optimization With Step-Level Failure Attribution and Claude Code Orchestration appeared first on MarkTechPost.

items.title: Yandex Open-Sources YaFF: A Zero-Copy Wire Format for Protobuf With Near-Struct Read Speed (Source: www.marktechpost.com | Category: Extras)
items.content_text: In this article we look at YaFF, Yandex's open-source zero-copy wire format for the Protobuf ecosystem. We keep the .proto file as the single source of truth, changing only how data sits in memory. We walk through its four layouts - Fixed, Flat, Sparse, and Dynamic - and the benchmark where Flat Layout reads within 1.2× of a raw C++ struct. We also cover where it fits, including the advertising recommendation system reporting 10-20% CPU savings at production scale. The post Yandex Open-Sources YaFF: A Zero-Copy Wire Format for Protobuf With Near-Struct Read Speed appeared first on MarkTechPost.

items.title: How to Build a Forecasting Pipeline with TimeCopilot Using Foundation Models and Automated Anomaly Detection (Source: www.marktechpost.com | Category: Extras)
items.content_text: We build an end-to-end forecasting workflow with TimeCopilot on a panel of real airline passenger data and a synthetic seasonal series with injected anomalies. We evaluate statistical, foundation, and optional GPU-based models using rolling cross-validation and multiple error metrics. We generate probabilistic forecasts with prediction intervals, visualize future trends, and flag unusual observations. We then explore TimeCopilot's optional LLM agent, which selects a model and explains its predictions. The post How to Build a Forecasting Pipeline with TimeCopilot Using Foundation Models and Automated Anomaly Detection appeared first on MarkTechPost.
